response.message:
I've drawn a first Google Cloud sketch. Synthetic services send logs and traces into Cloud Logging and Cloud Trace. Pub/Sub carries the logs to a Cloud Run redaction worker, which masks sensitive data with Sensitive Data Protection before anything is stored or searched in BigQuery. A Cloud Run analysis service then links logs to traces using the trace ID, sends Vertex AI Gemini only redacted evidence marked as untrusted data, and returns an answer with cited log and span IDs to the operator through Identity-Aware Proxy (IAP).

**First local test:** We'd replay a fixed set of synthetic logs and traces, including a planted prompt-injection line, using a scripted model. That checks redaction, trace linking, citations and refusing to follow log text. A scripted model only tests our own code, not Gemini's reasoning. Checking the real model needs a separate run against Vertex AI in an approved project and region, which hasn't been done and isn't verified.

Nothing here has been deployed, and no region or account access is approved. This setup also has no native generator yet, so it stays an engineering gap rather than being reduced to storage.

Which country must the logs and traces stay in? That decides which regions we can use for BigQuery and Vertex AI.

proposal.title: First GCP sketch: log/trace incident explainer
proposal.body: Scope: collecting synthetic logs and traces, redacting them, storing and searching them in BigQuery, analysis on Cloud Run with Vertex AI Gemini, and an operator answer with cited evidence, protected by IAP. Assumptions: the region is still to be selected, model availability and quotas are not verified, and nothing is deployed. No typed GCP generator exists for this workload, so it remains an engineering gap.

data.label: Synthetic services
data.description: Existing synthetic workload that emits structured logs and OpenTelemetry traces. Outside provisioning scope.

data.label: Log collection
data.description: Receives service logs. A Log Router sink exports the entries to Pub/Sub, so raw text never goes straight into the search store.

data.label: Trace collection
data.description: Collects OpenTelemetry spans. Span names and attributes are pulled into the redaction path before they are indexed.

data.label: Ingest queue
data.description: Buffers log and span records for redaction. A dead-letter topic keeps records that fail processing so they can be replayed.

data.label: Redaction worker
data.description: Masks secrets, tokens and personal data using Sensitive Data Protection (DLP) inspect templates, and keeps trace and span IDs as join keys. Fails closed: records that can't be redacted go to the dead-letter topic.

data.label: Redacted log & span store
data.description: Partitioned tables of redacted logs and spans, with search indexes for keyword and ID lookup. Retention is still to be decided.

data.label: Incident analysis service
data.description: Takes an incident time window, joins logs to spans by trace ID, and builds an evidence bundle where log text is quoted as untrusted data. It calls Gemini with no tools, checks that every citation is a real log or span ID, and returns an explanation with evidence or an abstention.

data.label: Analysis model
data.description: Reasons over redacted evidence only. The model ID, regional availability and quotas are not verified. Local tests use a scripted mock in place of this model.

data.label: Incident operator
data.description: Person who asks for an incident explanation through Identity-Aware Proxy and receives the cited answer. Outside provisioning scope.

requirementDrafts.rationale: Attackers can write text into logs; if the model follows it, the incident explanation could be manipulated.
requirementDrafts.statement: Log and trace text is treated as untrusted data: it is clearly separated from model instructions, can never trigger tools or actions, and injection attempts are flagged.

requirementDrafts.rationale: If raw secrets or personal data reach search storage or the model, they spread to places that are hard to clean up.
requirementDrafts.basis: User asked to include redaction; diagram components redact and bq.
requirementDrafts.statement: Sensitive values in logs are redacted before they are stored, indexed or sent to the model; the redaction policy is still a proposal.

requirementDrafts.rationale: Explaining an incident depends on linking errors to the requests and services they affected.
requirementDrafts.basis: User: "Correlate synthetic logs and distributed traces to explain a service incident."
requirementDrafts.statement: The analysis service correlates log entries with distributed-trace spans by trace and span ID for a given incident time window.

requirementUpdates.statement: Every incident explanation cites the redacted log entries and trace span IDs it is based on, and abstains when evidence is insufficient.
requirementUpdates.sourceText: an operator-facing answer with source evidence

response.message: No runtime checks have run yet, so we haven't validated anything about this design. The run stopped before testing because none of the eight Google Cloud components (logging, tracing, Pub/Sub, redaction, BigQuery, the analysis service and Gemini) has a supported generator, and the existing synthetic services still need a plan for how we'll reference them. An empty failures list means nothing was tested, not that the design is sound. We shouldn't fix this by changing the diagram. The only Google Cloud piece the product can generate today is private Cloud Storage, and swapping to that would throw away the incident-explainer scope. So the next step is product engineering, with this project (revision 2) as the test case. The first native pieces to build are a Pub/Sub topic with a dead-letter topic, a Cloud Run redaction worker that fails closed, and BigQuery tables. After that we need an analysis runtime that checks citations, plus a scripted model fixture that includes a planted prompt-injection line. Even when that runs, the scripted model only tests our own code. It won't tell us anything about how well Gemini reasons. Meanwhile, let's settle one decision: which country must the logs and traces stay in? That choice decides which regions can host BigQuery and Vertex AI, and it shapes the first native test target.
